encounters.cc: Shortness of breath, especially when lying down, during second pregnancy

lines: Shortness of breath, especially when lying down, during second pregnancy
This 31-year-old G2P1 with chronic hypertension and prior postpartum hemorrhage presents for second pregnancy with complaints of shortness of breath, especially when lying down.
She denies any cough, fever, or wheezing.
She has had an uncomplicated prenatal course thus far.
- Cesarean section (implied by possible repeat surgeries, but not explicitly stated - will leave as manual removal only)
- Labetalol 200 mg PO twice daily (adherence reported)
- Prenatal vitamin with iron 1 tablet PO daily
Alcohol: Rare social use, none during pregnancies.
On examination, her respiratory rate is 18 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation is 97% on room air.
Lung auscultation reveals clear breath sounds bilaterally.
Her abdomen is gravid, and fundal height is appropriate for gestational age.
A spirometry test yields the following results:
- Forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1): 3.2 L (normal)

encounters.cc: Progressive pain over pubic bone and bilateral groin areas worsened by walking or turning in bed

lines: Progressive pain over pubic bone and bilateral groin areas worsened by walking or turning in bed
This 31-year-old with chronic hypertension and postpartum hemorrhage returns for prenatal care following her January visit.
She reports that the pain is worse when walking, climbing stairs, or turning in bed.
She denies leakage of fluid, vaginal bleeding, or contractions.
- Cesarean section (implied by possible repeat surgeries, but not explicitly stated - will leave as manual removal only)
- Labetalol 200 mg PO twice daily (adherence reported)
- Prenatal vitamin with iron 1 tablet PO daily
Alcohol: Rare social use, none during pregnancies.
Her vital signs are within normal limits.
On physical examination, she has tenderness over the pubic symphysis and pain with passive abduction of her hips.
There is no erythema or edema over the joints, and her skin is intact.
Urinalysis is negative for protein, glucose, and infection.

encounters.cc: Routine prenatal visit with reports of decreased fetal movements over past two days

lines: Routine prenatal visit with reports of decreased fetal movements over past two days

The patient is a 31-year-old G2P1 female with chronic hypertension and a history of postpartum hemorrhage, now returning for prenatal care following prior visits for physiologic dyspnea and pelvic girdle pain.
She has a history of chronic hypertension, which has been poorly controlled during pregnancy despite adherence to labetalol therapy.
She reports decreased fetal movements over the past two days.
Her prenatal course has been otherwise unremarkable.
- Cesarean section (implied by possible repeat surgeries, but not explicitly stated - will leave as manual removal only)
- Prenatal vitamin with iron 1 tablet PO daily
Alcohol: Rare social use, none during pregnancies.
Fundal height is measuring 30 cm, which is less than expected for gestational age
An ultrasound is performed, which shows an estimated fetal weight in the 8th percentile for gestational age, but with a normal head circumference.
Doppler flow studies of the umbilical artery reveal increased resistance to blood flow.

encounters.cc: Persistent nausea, vomiting, and severe epigastric pain radiating to right upper quadrant

lines: Persistent nausea, vomiting, and severe epigastric pain radiating to right upper quadrant

This 31-year-old female with chronic hypertension, postpartum hemorrhage, and recent bilateral adrenal hemorrhage presents to the emergency department with a 24-hour history of persistent nausea, vomiting, and severe epigastric pain.
She reports that the pain radiates to her right upper quadrant.
Her pregnancy has been uncomplicated until now.
- Cesarean section (implied by possible repeat surgeries, but not explicitly stated - will leave as manual removal only)
- Labetalol 200 mg PO twice daily (adherence reported)
- Prenatal vitamin with iron 1 tablet PO daily
Alcohol: Rare social use, none during pregnancies.
On examination, her blood pressure is 145/95 mmHg, heart rate is 102 beats per minute, and she is afebrile.
Her skin and sclera are anicteric.
Abdominal examination reveals right upper quadrant tenderness without rebound or guarding.
Fetal monitoring shows a reactive fetal heart tracing.

encounters.cc: Sudden onset irregular abdominal pain at term gestation

lines: Sudden onset irregular abdominal pain at term gestation

The patient is a 31-year-old G2P1 with chronic hypertension and prior postpartum hemorrhage who presents to the labor and delivery unit at term following recent acute fatty liver of pregnancy and adrenal hemorrhage.
She reports a 1-hour history of sudden onset, irregular abdominal pain.
She denies any vaginal bleeding or leakage of fluid.
Her pregnancy has been uncomplicated, and she has received regular prenatal care.
- Cesarean section (implied by possible repeat surgeries, but not explicitly stated - will leave as manual removal only)
- Labetalol 200 mg PO twice daily (adherence reported)
- Prenatal vitamin with iron 1 tablet PO daily
Alcohol: Rare social use, none during pregnancies.
On examination, her blood pressure is 120/75 mmHg, heart rate is 88 beats per minute, and temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F)
Fetal heart monitoring shows a baseline fetal heart rate of 140 beats per minute with recurrent variable decelerations that decrease to 90 beats per minute with >50% of uterine contractions.
The decelerations are noted to have a rapid descent and return to baseline.
There is no evidence of maternal fever, tachycardia, or uterine tenderness.
The patient is placed in the left lateral decubitus position, and oxygen is administered via face mask.
Despite these measures, the fetal heart tracing does not improve.

encounters.cc: Sudden-onset severe abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding with significantly decreased fetal movements

lines: Sudden-onset severe abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding with significantly decreased fetal movements

This 31-year-old G2P1 female with chronic hypertension has a history of postpartum hemorrhage complicated by disseminated intravascular coagulation and antepartum complications including adrenal hemorrhage.
She presents to the emergency department with sudden-onset severe abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding that began 3 hours ago.
She reports that the pain is constant and not associated with uterine contractions.
Fetal movements have significantly decreased since the onset of symptoms.
Shortly after arrival, the patient develops oozing of blood from her intravenous catheter site and persistent vaginal bleeding.
- Umbilical cord compression causing recurrent variable decelerations (diagnosed 2022-11-15)
- Cesarean section (implied by possible repeat surgeries, but not explicitly stated - will leave as manual removal only)
- Labetalol 200 mg PO twice daily (adherence reported)
- Prenatal vitamin with iron 1 tablet PO daily
She does not smoke or use drugs.
Blood pressure is 90/58 mm Hg, pulse is 118/min
On examination, her uterus is firm and tender to palpation, and there is moderate vaginal bleeding.

encounters.cc: Dizziness and fatigue following motor vehicle collision

lines: Dizziness and fatigue following motor vehicle collision

The patient is a 32-year-old female with chronic hypertension on labetalol and a history of postpartum hemorrhage complicated by disseminated intravascular coagulation, who presents after a motor vehicle collision.
She reports that she was the restrained driver in a head-on collision at moderate speed.
Airbags were deployed, and she did not lose consciousness.
She complains of mild abdominal pain but no other specific symptoms.
- Umbilical cord compression causing recurrent variable decelerations (diagnosed 2022-11-15)
- Cesarean section (implied by possible repeat surgeries, but not explicitly stated - will leave as manual removal only)
- Labetalol 200 mg PO twice daily (adherence reported)
- Prenatal vitamin with iron 1 tablet PO daily
Alcohol: Rare social use, none during pregnancies.
Her blood pressure is 90/60 mmHg, heart rate is 120 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 22 breaths per minute, and temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F).
The patient's blood pressure drops to 85/55 mmHg despite receiving 2 liters of normal saline.
On examination, she appears pale and anxious.
Her skin is cool and clammy.
Abdominal examination reveals mild tenderness in the left upper quadrant with no rebound or guarding.
Focused Assessment with Sonography for Trauma (FAST) exam is negative for free fluid.
